subject: Urgent: ZagCom checkout timeouts — proxy queueing & peering path impact
messages:
From: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@zagcom.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.example; support@redwood.example
Cc: ops@zagcom.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 16:14:00 +0000
Subject: High error rate — checkout timeouts and spikes (urgent)

Dylan / Redwood support team,

We started seeing a sharp rise in checkout failures at ~09:00 PT this morning. Our telemetry shows a jump from ~0.5% 5xx to ~9% 502/504 errors for inference calls that power our recommendation checkout flow. Median tail latency has moved from ~120ms to 1.2s and some requests are timing out entirely. Impact: multiple customers are seeing abandoned carts.

Attached: zgc-request-logs.tar.gz (a sample of request traces and timestamps).

What we've observed from our side:
- Errors correlate with requests routed to your us-west-2 peering (peering-id: pcx-0a1b2c).
- Client-side retries amplify the traffic and we see connection resets and long TCP handshake times.

We need immediate triage and an ETA on mitigation. This is high business impact for ZagCom — please loop in whoever is needed (engineering + exec).

Carlos Rivera
Director, Platform Reliability
ZagCom

Subject: Fwd: High error rate — checkout timeouts and spikes (urgent)

Team — forwarding ZagCom's escalation. Quick triage notes and asks below. We should assume exec attention will be requested if we don't have an action within 30–60 minutes.

Immediate hypotheses (based on initial logs):
- Egress path saturation / proxy queueing on our us-west-2 NAT/proxy cluster. Queue depth on the nginx sidecars could be exploding under retry storms.
- VPC peering asymmetry: some sessions appear to be taking the primary peering path while replies route back via a different transit, causing connection stalls.
- DNS timeouts noted in the traces; upstream resolver rate-limiting could be compounding tail latency.

Please do the following now (owner in parentheses):
- Marcus: check egress NAT conntrack counters across the pool (us-west-2, prod-egress). Share recent conntrack logs and kernel drops.
- Naomi: inspect proxy sidecar queue metrics and nginx 503/504 spike timing. Capture heap/connection table stats.
- Soojin: query our DNS resolver logs for SERVFAIL/timeout patterns toward ZagCom's resolver IPs.
- Marissa: prep an exec note (2–3 bullets) for Sales/CS/Legal if customer requests credits.

I'll open a bridge for triage and loop in Marissa for exec comms.

Possible mitigations to try in parallel:
- Temporarily route ZagCom traffic via an alternate peering (cloudvendor-east) to test path divergence.
- Expand SNAT pool on the affected NAT gateway.
- Add short-lived firewall rule to drop suspicious long-lived idle sessions if conntrack is full.

I'll post updates to the thread. -- Dylan

Dylan Brooks
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Quick update from initial infra checks (prod-egress us-west-2):

What I see:
- NAT gateway metrics: conntrack table at ~94% across three nodes. Kernel logged nf_conntrack: table full events around 09:05-09:08 PT.
- iptables/nft counters show an increase in ESTABLISHED->RELATED connection drops consistent with conntrack eviction.
- Sample logs (timestamps normalized):
  [2027-06-07T16:04:12Z] upstream=10.18.4.22 status=504 proto=tcp rtt=1189ms
  [2027-06-07T16:04:13Z] resolver=8.8.8.8 status=SERVFAIL qname=recommend.fetch.zagcom.com

Root cause hypothesis:
- A sudden spike of long-lived multiplexed sessions from ZagCom + client retry storms is exhausting conntrack entries on our NAT nodes. With conntrack eviction, some packets are dropped mid-session and clients see 502/504.
- The peering path shows asymmetric routing (a small subset of return traffic is routed via an alternate transit that has a higher per-packet latency and occasional packet loss), >likely due to recent BGP weight changes at a partner. That asymmetry increases TCP retransmits and stretches session lifetimes, worsening conntrack pressure.
- DNS SERVFAILs appear to be upstream rate-limiting; this increases application retry churn and amplifies the volume hitting our egress proxies.

Immediate actions taken (completed):
- Increased conntrack table size on two low-latency NAT nodes (hotfix) and cleared stale entries to free headroom.
- Deployed a temporary SNAT pool expansion on us-west-2 to spread translations across additional nodes.
- Added request-rate filters at the nginx sidecars to reject immediate retry storms (503 fast-fail with retry-after header).

Recommended next steps (near-term):
- Route ZagCom traffic to alternate peering (cloudvendor-east) for 30–60 minutes to validate path stability. (Dylan/Network ops)
- Coordinate with cloud vendor NOC to confirm recent BGP weight adjustments and request rollback if they match our incident window. (Network ops)
- Work with ZagCom to reduce aggressive client-side retries as a stability measure while we stabilize egress.

I'll keep digging into kernel logs and BGP metrics. If conntrack usage continues to grow we'll need a planned capacity increase for the customer's dedicated peering.

-- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident update and exec sync proposal — ZagCom checkout impact (actions taken)

Carlos / ZagCom team / Cloud NOC,

Thanks for the quick signal and patience. Summary of what we did and next steps:

What we observed:
- Brief period of conntrack exhaustion on us-west-2 NATs that coincided with client retry storms and asymmetric peering routing.
- DNS SERVFAILs from upstream resolvers increased retry churn and contributed to higher egress load.

Actions completed (timeline):
- 09:10 PT: Increased conntrack headroom, expanded SNAT pool on affected nodes (hotfix).
- 09:18 PT: Applied nginx fast-fail filter to short-circuit retry storms.
- 09:40 PT: Rerouted ZagCom traffic via alternate peering (cloudvendor-east) — observed immediate drop in 5xx and tail latency.

Impact: Around 09:45 PT we saw 5xx drop from ~9% back toward baseline and median latency return to ~150ms. Checkout errors for ZagCom reduced to low single digits within 20–30 minutes of the mitigation.

Next steps / requests:
- We recommend a short joint post-mortem call with ZagCom SRE + Redwood Network + Cloud NOC to confirm BGP weights and make the alternate peering route permanent if desired. Proposed time: today 17:00 PT.
- Marcus will prepare kernel-level metrics and conntrack graphs for the call.
- We suggest ZagCom temporarily soften retry backoff parameters on client SDKs for the next 24 hours while we provision a longer-term egress scale plan.
- Marissa will lead customer exec comms on credits and SLA exceptions if requested.

Executive note (Marissa):
- We will offer a one-off credit for the impacted window and prioritize capacity increases for ZagCom's peering.

Carlos — would you be available for the 17:00 PT call? If yes, I'll send a calendar invite and include our Head of Network/Cloud NOC.

Attachments: pcap-sample.txt (edge TCP handshake snippet)
